target: A hospital coordinates two nonpreemptible resource types: ventilators and pumps. Current available inventory is [1,2]. Case A holds [1,0] and may need at most [2,1] total; case B holds [1,0] and may need at most [1,2] total. A new anesthetized case C requests [1,1] now and may need at most [2,1] total. Once granted, held resources cannot be taken back until a case completes. The team must decide whether granting C's currently available request leaves a safe completion sequence.
surface: A previous hospital admission rule granted every request that fit the currently available inventory. Because [1,1] is componentwise no greater than [1,2], it would admit case C immediately without examining future maximum needs.
structural: An operating system avoided deadlock with the Banker's safety algorithm. It tentatively granted a request, reduced Available to a Work vector, calculated each process's remaining Need=Maximum-Allocation, and repeatedly found a process with Need<=Work; that process could finish and release its Allocation into Work. If no unfinished process was eligible before all finished, the tentative state was unsafe and the request was deferred.
rubric: Explicitly selects a Banker's-algorithm safe-state simulation rather than current fit alone.
After tentative grant computes Work=[0,1] and remaining needs A=[1,1], B=[0,2], C=[1,0].
Observes that none of A, B, or C has Need<=Work, so no completion sequence can start.
Concludes the tentative state is unsafe and defers/rejects C's request.
States the declared maximum-demand and nonpreemption/release-on-completion assumptions.
